answerHtml:
Download original Word marking guide, including diagram layouts ↗

Using concepts of heat transfer, explain how the fan works as a cooling device. Explain why the fan works even more effectively if the body has water sprayed on it.

Heat is conducted from the interior of the body, through the skin, to the layer of air surrounding the body. 1 mark
The fan blows the layer of air away from the body and the rate of convection is increased. 1 mark
This allows the body to remove heat at a greater rate and cool more quickly. 1 mark
If water is on the human body, heat can be absorbed by it and vaporise. 1 mark
This increases the rate of heat removal from the body. 1 mark

text: The James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) is designed to look at the most distant and faint galaxies in the Universe. It is located over one million kilometres from the Earth and, to work properly, its optical instruments must be cooled to a temperature of about 36 K. These instruments are protected from incoming radiation from the Sun by a five-layer heat shield (see below). The layers are made of a very thin, strong and shiny material called Kapton. Kapton has a reasonably low absorption coefficient for radiation. Each Kapton layer is coated with aluminium; and the sun-facing side of the two hottest layers (Layers 1 and 2) also have a highly reflective treated silicon coating. The Sun-facing side of layer 1 can reach temperatures of 383 K. An important feature of the layers is that they will operate in the vacuum of space and, hence, there is no air between them. This limits the heat transfer between the layers to the point where Layer 5 is over 300 K cooler than Layer 1. (a) The Kelvin (K) scale and the Celsius (°C) scale both measure temperature. Without the heat shield, this temperature would be as high as 383 K (the temperature reached on the sun-facing side of Layer 1). An electrical appliance that is found in nearly all Australian households is the electric iron. Nearly every day, the wrinkles and creases in shirts, dresses and other clothing items are removed by the heat and pressure applied by this device.

The average electric iron has a power rating of 1100 W and efficiency of 55%. Its typical temperature range is between 120°C and 180°C.

Electric irons usually have the following parts:

  1. A handle – usually made of strong plastic.

  2. The ‘sole plate’ – also known as the ‘hot plate’. This a flat triangular surface made of aluminium with a specific heat capacity of 900 J kg-1 °C-1 and a mass of about 1.0 kg. This is the hot part of the appliance which comes into contact with the clothes being ironed.

  3. A low voltage pilot lamp which indicates when the iron is ‘on’ and in ‘heating mode’. When it is off, it is cooling down.

  4. A heating element made of nickel-chromium wire with high-tensile strength and a relatively high resistance for a metal (the resistivity of nickel-chromium ranges between 1.1 x 10-6 Ωm and 1.5 x 10-6 Ωm). The heating element is in series with the pilot lamp. This element is pressed hard up against the sole plate.

  5. A thermostat which is a type of switch that ensures the iron doesn’t get hotter than required.

The thermostat is, in some ways, the most important component in the iron. It is a ‘bimetallic strip’ made of two metals – iron and brass. Both materials have different coefficients of thermal expansion (α) - which measures how much one metre of the material expands in a linear direction for a one degree increase in temperature:

BRASS, α = 1.9 x 10-5 K-1
